stem.text: Let \( f(x) = - 4 \left(x + 2\right)^{3} \sin{\left(\frac{1}{x + 2} \right)} + 2 \) for \( x \ne -2 \). Find \( \lim_{x \to -2} f(x) \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: The limit is 2, because \( 2 - 4 \left|{x + 2}\right|^{3} \le f(x) \le 4 \left|{x + 2}\right|^{3} + 2 \) for \( x \ne -2 \) and both bounds approach 2 as x approaches -2.

worked_solution.text: Multiplying by the nonnegative quantity \( 4 \left|{x + 2}\right|^{3} \) and adding 2 gives \( 2 - 4 \left|{x + 2}\right|^{3} \le f(x) \le 4 \left|{x + 2}\right|^{3} + 2 \). The factor \( - 4 \left(x + 2\right)^{3} \) can be negative, so its absolute value is used to keep the inequality true.
Both bounds are continuous, so their limits as x approaches -2 are both 2.
